name: Georgios Alexopoulos

neurosurgery_residency.institution: Saint Louis University (SSM Health), dismissed before completion

other_training.institution: Papageorgiou GH Thessaloniki / G. Gennimatas GH Athens, Greece

current_position: Attending neurosurgeon at Panarkadiko General Hospital (Tripoli, Greece) and HYGEIA/MITERA (Athens); co-founder of Neuroknife. Holds a Greek neurosurgery specialty title (2025) and is European Board certified.
evidence: St. Louis Record (Jul 17 2025) reports on his lawsuit against SSM Saint Louis University Hospital. He was 'involuntarily dismissed from SSM Saint Louis University Hospital's neurosurgery residency program on July 8, 2024, just months before completing his seven-year training', after academic probation. The complaint says he 'remains unable to practice medicine' (in the US). His Neuroknife CV lists 'Neurosurgery Resident - Saint Louis University ... (2018-2024)' with no completion claim. It also lists earlier Greek neurosurgery residency (2012-2016), a UIC general surgery year (2016-17), a Boston Children's pediatric neurosurgery clinical fellowship (2017-18), a Greek neurosurgery specialty title (2025), and current attending posts in Tripoli and Athens.
notes: Conflict resolved: he did NOT complete SLU. He was dismissed July 8 2024 at the start of what would have been PGY-7, which agrees with current_outcome 'LEFT -> did not complete'. 'SLU 2018-2024' on Doximity and his bio covers his time as a resident, not graduation. He did not transfer to another US residency. He went back to Greece and got the Greek neurosurgery specialty title, so he still practices neurosurgery abroad. The verdict is 'left_medicine_or_other' as the closest fit ('other' = dismissed and now practicing abroad); it does not mean he left medicine. The lawsuit (allegations of discrimination/retaliation) was pending as of Jul 2025.
